Find, to the **nearest degree**, the measure of the obtuse angle $X.$

$m∠X≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
The Law of Sines states that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡X}{x}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡Z}{z}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
x=14,\,m∠Z={40}^{∘},\,z=10,
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡X}{14} & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{40}^{∘}}{10} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡X & =14\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{40}^{∘}}{10} \\  & =\frac{14\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{40}^{∘}}{10} \\  & ≈\frac{14\cdot 0.643}{10} \\  & ≈0.900,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠X & ≈\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.900)≈{64.158}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

But this is less than ${90}^{∘}.$ To get the true value of $X,$ we subtract our answer from ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
m∠X≈{180}^{∘}-{64.158}^{∘}≈{116}^{∘},
$$

rounded to the nearest degree.
